refentry.refsect1:
&reftitle.description;
Socket context options are available for all wrappers that work over sockets, like tcp, http and ftp.

&reftitle.options;
bindto
Used to specify the IP address (either IPv4 or IPv6) and/or the port number that PHP will use to access the network. The syntax is ip:port for IPv4 addresses, and [ip]:port for IPv6 addresses. Setting the IP or the port to 0 will let the system choose the IP and/or port.
As FTP creates two socket connections during normal operation, the port number cannot be specified using this option.
backlog
Used to limit the number of outstanding connections in the socket's listen queue.
This is only applicable to stream_socket_server.
ipv6_v6only
Overrides the OS default regarding mapping IPv4 into IPv6.
This is important in particular when trying to listen on IPv4 addresses separately while there exists a binding on [::].
This is only applicable to stream_socket_server.
so_reuseport
Allows multiple bindings to a same ip:port pair, even from separate processes.
This is only applicable to stream_socket_server.
so_reuseaddr
Whether to set SO_REUSEADDR on the socket, which allows binding to an ip:port pair while connections of a previous socket bound to it are still in the TIME_WAIT state, for example when a server is restarted. On Windows, it also allows binding to an ip:port pair that another socket is bound to.
Defaults to &true;. When set to &false;, SO_REUSEADDR is not set, and on Windows SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE is set instead, which prevents other sockets from binding to the same ip:port pair.
This is only applicable to stream_socket_server.
so_broadcast
Enables sending and receiving data to/from broadcast addresses.
This is only applicable to stream_socket_server.
so_rcvbuf
The size of the receive buffer of the socket in bytes (SO_RCVBUF). The value must be an integer between 1 and 2147483647; otherwise, opening the stream fails.
The operating system may round, cap, or otherwise adjust the requested size. Setting this option may also turn off the automatic sizing of the buffer by the operating system.
This is only applicable to TCP and UDP sockets.
so_sndbuf
The size of the send buffer of the socket in bytes (SO_SNDBUF). The value must be an integer between 1 and 2147483647; otherwise, opening the stream fails.
The operating system may round, cap, or otherwise adjust the requested size. Setting this option may also turn off the automatic sizing of the buffer by the operating system.
This is only applicable to TCP and UDP sockets.
so_linger
The number of seconds for which closing the socket waits for unsent data to be sent (SO_LINGER). A positive value enables lingering for that many seconds. Zero or a negative value disables lingering, so that closing the socket returns immediately and the remaining data is sent in the background. Values above 65535 are treated as 65535.
With stream_socket_server, it is set on the listening socket and inherited by the accepted connections.
This is only applicable to TCP sockets.
so_keepalive
Setting this option to &true; enables TCP keepalive (SO_KEEPALIVE): probes are sent over a connection that has been idle for some time, so that a peer which is no longer reachable is detected and the connection is dropped. The probes are configured by tcp_keepidle, tcp_keepintvl, and tcp_keepcnt; the settings of the operating system are used for those that are not set.
With stream_socket_server, the keepalive options are set on the listening socket and inherited by the accepted connections.
This is only applicable to TCP sockets.
tcp_keepidle
The number of seconds a connection must be idle before the first keepalive probe is sent (TCP_KEEPIDLE, or TCP_KEEPALIVE on macOS).
This is only applicable to TCP sockets, and only has an effect if so_keepalive is enabled. It is ignored on platforms that do not support it.
tcp_keepintvl
The number of seconds between consecutive keepalive probes (TCP_KEEPINTVL).
This is only applicable to TCP sockets, and only has an effect if so_keepalive is enabled. It is ignored on platforms that do not support it.
tcp_keepcnt
The number of unanswered keepalive probes after which the connection is dropped (TCP_KEEPCNT).
This is only applicable to TCP sockets, and only has an effect if so_keepalive is enabled. It is ignored on platforms that do not support it.
tcp_nodelay
Setting this option to &true; will set SOL_TCP,NO_DELAY=1 appropriately, thus disabling the TCP Nagle algorithm.

&reftitle.changelog;
&Version; &Description;
8.6.0
Added so_reuseaddr, so_rcvbuf, so_sndbuf, so_linger, so_keepalive, tcp_keepidle, tcp_keepintvl, and tcp_keepcnt.
7.1.0
Added tcp_nodelay.
7.0.1
Added ipv6_v6only.
